newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen down in the short-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen down in the short-term.

text.p: London cocoa futures may extend losses in the short-term but support should hold at 995-980 stg area basis the key December contract, technical analysts said.
Traders called the market 9-10 stg lower on Wednesday after December slumped to a six-month low of $1,361 in New York.
Fuelling the downside this week was unconfirmed reports that one private U.S. forecaster raised its estimate for the Ivorian main crop up to about 930,000 tonnes.
A UK pod counter is expected to release its assessment of the Ivorian crop development later this week.
Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said London cocoa could see more downside in the short term, but RSIs were approaching oversold levels and nearby support should hold.
"I wouldn't expect a test of 965 support," Haylor said.
But the technical picture remained weak after the market broke through a sequence of key support levels last week and slipped through 1,010 stg basis December on Tuesday.
Haylor said with resistance at 1,020 stg -- around the 40-day moving average -- a good trading strategy would be to sell the market with a stop placed at 1,020 stg.
Moving averages were above the market and bearish, Haylor added.
Ivorian output prospects are said to have improved slightly after the crop escaped much damage from heavy rains in early July but pod setting remains unimpressive, cocoa analysts said.
First arrivals may not be as late as initially estimated, but they could drastically slow down in December.
A possible record delivery of the September contract is expected to go smoothly from Monday with abundant cocoa waiting to be tendered at the Exchange, traders said.
One trading house is expected to take delivery of about 30,000 lots, or 300,000 tonnes of cocoa.
